title: Ab initio characterization of protein molecular dynamics with AI2BMD

nodes.text: AI2BMD is an AI-based ab initio biomolecular dynamics system that simulates full-atom large biomolecules (>10,000 atoms) with ab initio accuracy using a protein fragmentation scheme combined with a machine learning force field.
nodes.evidence: we introduce an artificial intelligence-based ab initio biomolecular dynamics system (AI2BMD) that can efficiently simulate full-atom large biomolecules with ab initio accuracy

nodes.text: A generalizable protein fragmentation approach splits any protein into overlapped dipeptide 'protein units' of just 21 kinds, each with 12-36 atoms, making DFT data generation and MLFF training tractable while generalizing across proteins.
nodes.evidence: Our fragmentation approach contains only 21 kinds of protein unit, and all protein units have similar and moderate numbers of atoms (range from 12 to 36)

nodes.text: The AI2BMD potential is based on the ViSNet architecture, which encodes physics-informed molecular representations and computes four-body interactions with linear time complexity for energy and force prediction.
nodes.evidence: The AI2BMD potential, based on ViSNet7, calculates the energy and atomic forces... The model encodes physics-informed molecular representations and calculates four-body interactions with linear time complexity

nodes.text: The simulation system couples the ML potential with an explicit polarizable solvent modeled by the AMOEBA force field via polarizable embedding.
nodes.evidence: we developed an MD simulation system with a polarizable solvent described by the AMOEBA force field16

nodes.text: Classical MD is fast but lacks chemical accuracy, while quantum chemistry methods like DFT reach chemical accuracy but cannot scale to large biomolecules; AI2BMD is positioned to bridge this gap by delivering ab initio accuracy at far lower cost.
nodes.evidence: Classical molecular dynamics simulation is fast but lacks chemical accuracy... density functional theory can reach chemical accuracy but cannot scale to support large biomolecules

nodes.text: Training an MLFF on samples from one kind of protein and simulating other kinds usually leads to simulation collapse, motivating the universal fragmentation approach for generalization.
nodes.evidence: simulating other kinds of protein with the MLFF usually leads to simulation collapse12

nodes.text: AI2BMD simulates faster than the AI-driven systems DPMD and Allegro and the AMOEBA force field (Tinker), and avoids out-of-memory errors on large proteins that DPMD and Allegro hit on an A6000 GPU.
nodes.evidence: AI2BMD exhibits a faster simulation speed, except for the smallest protein chignolin, than DPMD... both DPMD and Allegro encountered an 'out-of-memory' error on an A6000 GPU card for some large proteins, whereas AI2BMD worked well

nodes.text: On protein units, the AI2BMD potential achieved energy MAE of 0.045 kcal/mol versus 3.198 for the MM force field (about two orders of magnitude better) and force MAE of 0.078 versus 8.125 kcal/mol/Angstrom.
nodes.evidence: AI2BMD: 0.045 kcal mol−1, MM: 3.198 kcal mol−1... force MAE (0.078 kcal mol−1 Å−1) compared to MM (8.125 kcal mol−1 Å−1)

nodes.text: Across nine proteins (175 to 13,728 atoms), AI2BMD's potential-energy errors closely matched DFT/fragment-DFT references (0.038 and 7.18e-3 kcal/mol per atom) while MM hovered around 0.2 kcal/mol per atom.
nodes.evidence: MM... consistently hovered around 0.2 kcal mol−1 per atom, whereas AI2BMD achieved a much lower value (0.038 kcal mol−1 per atom

nodes.text: AI2BMD reduces compute time by several orders of magnitude versus DFT; e.g., a Trp-cage step took 0.072 s versus 21 min by DFT, and aminopeptidase N (13,728 atoms) took 2.610 s while DFT was estimated to exceed 254 days (>6 orders slower).
nodes.evidence: it was 2.610 s, and DFT calculations were not feasible with the estimated time exceeding 254 days, which would be more than 6 orders slower than AI2BMD

nodes.text: With hundreds of nanoseconds of dynamics, AI2BMD derived 3J couplings matching NMR experiments, captured protein folding/unfolding, and produced free-energy and thermodynamic estimates (e.g., melting temperatures) aligned with experiment.
nodes.evidence: deriving accurate 3J couplings that match nuclear magnetic resonance experiments... enables precise free-energy calculations for protein folding, and the estimated thermodynamic properties are well aligned with experiments

nodes.text: In hydrogen-bond sampling/scanning of an asparagine dipeptide in water, AI2BMD's solute-solvent distance and energy distributions matched QM-MM closely while MM deviated, showing accurate solvent-effect modeling.
nodes.evidence: AI2BMD also demonstrated an energy distribution much more consistent with QM–MM than MM in the hydrogen-bond scanning

nodes.text: AI2BMD detects different phenomena than molecular mechanics (MM), suggesting it can complement wet-lab experiments and reveal dynamic bioactivity processes inaccessible today.
nodes.evidence: detects different phenomena than molecular mechanics (MM)... enable biomedical research that is impossible to conduct at present
